flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: I just played the King's Indian move and you gave me a blank gold star. g6 is not a random pawn nudge — it prepares ...Bg7 and the whole fianchetto plan. If this is 'the strongest move' with zero reasons, you are teaching me that openings are vibes.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-rook to e8 is playable, but moving your pawn to e5 would be better because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: I cannot 'likely take a pawn' with ...e5. That is the thematic King's Indian break, fighting for the center and asking d4-d5 or dxe5. You invented a capture and skipped the only opening idea I needed on this move. Re8 is a real inaccuracy; the because-clause is a lie.

flags.quote: Moving your f3-knight to e1 is playable, but moving your pawn to e5 would be better because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: Same canned 'likely take a pawn' on White's e5. e5 hits the f6-knight and clamps the center; it does not scoop a hanging pawn. Two plies, one fake tactic. I stop trusting 'because' after this.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is the moment the King's Indian becomes a closed game — White locks the center and the plans split (queenside vs kingside). You printed a verdict and no reasons. If you only get one teaching sentence in this opening, it should be this pawn.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: b4 kicks the c5-knight. That is the entire move. You had a kicked-piece fact sitting in the pipeline and still said nothing. I learn that pawn pushes are 'strongest' for no reason, then later get punished for not noticing attacks.

flags.quote: Moving your e1-knight to d3 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: e4 is not hanging here — f3 and Nc3 already cover it. Nd3 is the standard Ne1–d3 reroute, supporting c5/e5 and the queenside. You hallucinated a rescue. Wrong because-clause on a book maneuver.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: ...f5 is the kingside break I have been aiming at since ...Nh5, and your hidden reason is pawn_shield — as if I just wrecked my own king. You then surface nothing. Attack tagged as shield damage, lesson deleted. Cool.

flags.quote: Moving your e3-bishop to f2 is the strongest move because it saves your f2-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: The bishop was on e3, attacked by ...f4. It is not a 'f2-bishop' until after I move it. You named the destination and called that a save. This is the retreat-label bug and it sounds like a joke.

flags.quote: Moving your a6-knight to b8 is the strongest move because it saves your b8-knight from capture.
flags.critique: Again: the knight is on a6, kicked by b5, running to b8. There is no b8-knight to save. You also stuffed backward_pawn onto a knight retreat. I cannot learn piece safety from copy that fails chessboard geometry.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c6 is the strongest move because it unveils an attack from your bishop on the black pawn.
flags.critique: c6 is a wedge: it hits d7, wrecks the queenside, and makes a protected passer dream. Your discovered-bishop-on-a-pawn story is the wrong movie. Teach the pawn cramp, not a ghost unveil.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on c6 with your b-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: This is a recapture on a pawn I just lost, and your reasons include wins_material. Recapturing even is not winning material. 'Undefended' is technically the SEE line and pedagogically greedy-sounding on an obvious recapture.

flags.quote: Moving your d7-knight to f6 is the strongest move because it saves your f6-knight from capture.
flags.critique: The hanging knight is on d7, staring at the c6 pawn. I move it to f6. You congratulate me for saving the piece that exists only after the move. Third copy of the destination-square bug; I am not laughing anymore.

flags.quote: Moving your b5-knight to c3 is the strongest move because it saves your c3-knight from capture.
flags.critique: a6 kicked the b5-knight. It retreats to c3. You did not save a c3-knight; you un-hanged the b5-knight. Four retreats, four times you name the landing square. This template is broken.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to e1 is a mistake, but moving your a1-rook to b1 would be better because your rook can use an open file.
flags.critique: 141 centipawns for 'put a rook on an open file' is textbook filler. You never say what Qe1 actually spoiled — the kingside is exploding with ...g4, and the queen wandered off. Open-file is true and useless.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You begged for ...g4 on Bh8, Ng7, and h5, then when I finally play it you have nothing. This is the lever that pries f3 and the white king. Empty strongest-move after a four-ply campaign is contempt.

flags.quote: You are still winning, but taking the pawn on g4 with your f-pawn puts it at risk of attack from the black c8-bishop and f6-knight. A better move would have been moving your king to h1.
flags.critique: +226 to +94 is not 'still winning'; you just opened my king and hung the new g-pawn. Kh1 is the same un-explained suggestion as last ply. 'Puts it at risk' never names that I ripped my own shield.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to g7 is a blunder, but taking the bishop on g4 with your c8-bishop would be better because the bishop was undefended and you take the defender of the white queen.
flags.critique: Bg4 is hanging — that part is the lesson. It is not defending the white queen on d1. You glued a removed-defender clause onto the wrong unit and turned a clean 'take the free bishop' into nonsense.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on c8 with your g4-bishop is the strongest move because you take the defender of the black pawn.
flags.critique: I took a bishop that Qg7 abandoned. Which black pawn did Bc8 defend that now hangs? You keep saying 'defender of X' when X is whatever the detector pointed at. The real sentence is: you win the piece they left loose.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on f1 with your e3-knight is the strongest move because you come out a bishop ahead.
flags.critique: I took a rook with a knight. That is the exchange, about two pawns, not a bishop. Your materialLabel maps +200 SEE to 'a bishop' and now I think I won a minor piece. I can see the captured rook on the board.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on f1 with your king is a mistake because the knight was undefended. A better move would have been taking the knight on f1 with your queen because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: If it was undefended, taking it is not the problem — taking it with the king is. You used a capture benefit as the mistake because. Qxf1 keeps the king on g1; 'pin the pawn to the rook' is the same pin spam you will paste for the rest of the game.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to f6 is a blunder, but moving your pawn to f3 would be better because you can likely pin the pawn to the queen.
flags.critique: 774 centipawns and you still do not mention the white king on f1. ...f3 rips g2, threatens mate ideas, and forces the king. 'Likely pin the pawn to the queen' is a hallucinated tactic. This is the game, and you missed it.

flags.quote: Moving your c3-knight to b5 is a blunder, but moving your queen to f3 would be better because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: I dropped a +667 position to −330 and you sold me a pin. Qf3 is about the king, f4, and not wandering a knight while the kingside is on fire. A 997-centipawn swing with a phrase-bank pin is malpractice.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on c7 with your b5-knight hands the opponent the advantage because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: You cannot tell me the capture is bad because the pawn was free. That is inverted: greed is the blunder, not the hanging-ness. wins_material leaked into a hands-advantage sentence and now 'undefended' means both good and catastrophic.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h3 is a blunder, but moving your queen to f3 would be better.
flags.critique: 1439 centipawns, no because, Qf3 for the nth time. If the engine line is always Qf3, teach what Qf3 does to ...f3/...f4 and the king on f1. A naked 'would be better' on a game-losing pawn nudge is a shrug.

flags.quote: Moving your g3-rook to e3 lets white force checkmate in 9 moves. This lets white force checkmate in 9 moves. A better move would have been moving your pawn to f3.
flags.critique: You said the mate sentence twice. I noticed. You still never show the mate idea or why ...f3 was the emergency break for half the ending. Mate-in-9 is the one fact I needed; repeating it is not teaching.

suggestions.title: Name retreated pieces from the origin square
suggestions.detail: saves_piece is filled with movedPiece after the retreat, so ownedPhrase prints f2-bishop / b8-knight / f6-knight / c3-knight. Pass the from-square unit (or drop the square and say 'your bishop'). A 1200 hears tautology and concludes the coach cannot see the board. This game alone repeats the bug on Bf2, Nb8, Ndf6, and Nc3.

suggestions.title: Stop using capture benefits as mistake reasons
suggestions.detail: Kxf1 is a mistake 'because the knight was undefended'; Nbxc7 'hands the advantage because the pawn was undefended'. pickProblemReasons / playedBecause must not lead with wins_material or hanging-target-is-free when classification is mistake/blunder. Explain the king walk, the missed recapture, or the counterattack. Learners treat 'undefended' as a reason to take, then get told taking is a blunder.

suggestions.title: Kill likely-capture and likely-pin filler
suggestions.detail: verifyLikelyTactics still lets 'you can likely take a pawn' through on ...e5/e5 (40cp band) and 'likely pin the pawn to the queen/rook' onto ...f3 and Qf3 for plies 67–77. Require the PV's first move to actually capture or pin, or demand a hanging target this ply. Opening breaks and king-file crams are not tactics. This is the #1 trust-killer.

suggestions.title: Call rook-for-knight the exchange
suggestions.detail: materialLabel maps 200cp to 'a bishop' and 250cp to 'a knight'. Nxf1 (rook, knight recapturable) becomes 'a bishop ahead'. hangingLossCopy already special-cases 180–220 as 'the exchange' — reuse that in wins_material copy. Anyone who just took a rook will laugh at 'bishop'.

suggestions.title: Teach ...f3/...g4 as king-file breaks
suggestions.detail: This game's climax is ...g4 then ...f3 against a king on f1/g1. Add a facts check: pawn advance that opens the file/diagonal toward the enemy king (or forces a king reply) outranks likely pin. Phrase-bank: 'it rips open the king' / 'it forces the king to deal with the pawn'. Would have fixed plies 44–50, 68, 71–78 in one detector.

suggestions.title: Emit a kick when a pawn attacks a piece
suggestions.detail: kicked_by_pawn only fires when the moved piece lands on a pawn's capture square. Pawn moves that kick (b4 vs Nc5, b5 vs Na6, a6 vs Nb5) currently get empty 'strongest move'. Detect opponent pieces newly attacked by the moved pawn and surface 'it kicks the knight'. Beginners miss pawn attacks; this is the easiest true sentence in the KID middlegame.

suggestions.title: Don't name a defender of the wrong piece
suggestions.detail: removed_defender rendered 'defender of the white queen' on Bxg4 and 'defender of the black pawn' on Bxc8 — both false. Gate the reason on newlyHanging actually being attacked and previously defended by the captured unit. If the capture is just a hanging piece, use hanging/wins_material only. Wrong X in 'defender of X' is worse than silence.

suggestions.title: Don't tag attacking pawn storms as shield damage
suggestions.detail: pawnShieldDamage fires on ...f5 and ...g5 (attacking KID storms) and then either hides the reason or, on ...h5, scolds king cover. Skip pawn_shield when the pawn move gains space toward the opponent king or is the known break (...e5/...f5/...g4, d5 closing). Add a closed-center / space reason for d5 so the structure moment is not a blank verdict.

whatWorked: Castling copy on plies 10 and 13 actually explains king plus rook — rare concrete because-clause.
Ply 19 f3: e4 really was hanging to two knights; 'saves your pawn from capture' was the right lesson.
Ply 26 suggested Nf4 fork of Nd3 and Be2 is real tactics, named both targets.
Ply 51 Bh4 pin of the knight to the queen is the correct geometric fact.
Ply 63's Rb8 skewer (rook exposing the e8-knight) and ply 64 Ne3 fork of queen and rook are the coaching I wanted all game.
Ply 69 Bxf6 skewer of queen and bishop on the long diagonal is clean and true.
Simple hanging-pawn takes (Nxa6, hxg4) are honest when they stay at 'the pawn was undefended'.
